title: Post-offer candidate experience: communication cadence and templates
content:
Purpose:
This doc defines a pragmatic, repeatable 10-step communication cadence for candidates from verbal offer through first 30 days. Goal is to reduce drop-off after offer, improve perceived care and clarity, and surface acceptance blockers early.

Scope and audience:
- Audience: hiring managers, recruiters, people-ops coordinators, hiring committee.
- Scope: post-offer communications (verbal offer, written offer, pre-sign, post-sign, preboarding to day 30 handoff to onboarding). Not the full onboarding curriculum.

Key success metrics (recommended to track):
- Offer acceptance rate (by role and channel)
- Time from verbal offer to signature
- Candidate NPS pre-first-day
- Unplanned declines (reasons logged)
- % of hires with first-week access ready on day 1

Owner and responsibilities:
- People Ops (owner): overall cadence maintenance, analytics, templates, weekly audit
- Recruiter: primary exec of cadence steps 1–6, customize templates, log candidate signals
- Hiring Manager: outreach at steps 3 and 5, provide role/team welcome note and first-week plan
- Onboarding (hand-off): receives final checklist at step 9 and owns first-day logistics

10-step cadence (timeline relative to verbal offer):
1) T0: Verbal offer (phone) 
   - Who: Recruiter + Hiring Manager present if possible
   - Action: deliver core offer terms, confirm target start window, ask for questions and timeline to decide
   - Log: add verbal-offer timestamp in ATS and set next contact date

2) T0+0–4 hours: Written offer email (formal PDF)
   - Who: Recruiter
   - Action: send signed offer letter PDF, benefits snapshot, link to offer FAQ doc, include acceptance instructions and point of contact
   - Template subject line: "Redwood Inference — Offer for {{role}}"

3) T0+24–48 hours: Manager welcome note (short)
   - Who: Hiring Manager
   - Action: send 2–3 sentence welcome + what the first week looks like and a personal calendar invite for a 30-min check-in (if candidate signs)

4) T0+72 hours: Check-in call / open Q&A (optional, schedule if candidate asks)
   - Who: Recruiter or Hiring Manager
   - Action: surface negotiation blockers, visa/relocation, background-check expectations, and confirm any outstanding questions

5) Pre-sign (if candidate requests time): T0+up to 7 days: "Decision support" email
   - Who: Recruiter
   - Action: short summary of package, link to benefits deep-dive, peer intro option, and offer to arrange manager call about growth/roadmap

6) Post-sign immediate (T_sign+0–4 hours): Welcome + next steps
   - Who: Recruiter + People Ops
   - Action: confirmation of signature receipt, congratulations, outline of preboarding tasks (forms, payroll, equipment), single checklist link 
   - Include: expected timeline for background check, access provisioning, and point-of-contact for logistics

7) Pre-boarding sequence (T_sign+1–14 days): automated & human touches
   - Automated: weekly checklist emails (forms, documentation submission, pre-reading links)
   - Human: People Ops reach-out by day 3 after sign to confirm forms and answer questions
   - Deliverable: candidate completes background paperwork and submits required IDs by day 7 wherever possible

8) 5 days before start: manager sends first-week plan + team intro doc
   - Who: Hiring Manager
   - Action: share a small agenda for days 1–5, expected deliverables, and 3 people to meet on day 1. Provide Slack channel invitation if available.

9) Day 0 (24–48 hours before start): Onboarding handoff
   - Who: People Ops -> Onboarding team
   - Action: send completed candidate checklist, equipment status, access status, and a red/amber/green readiness flag. Add candidate to new-hire tracker.

10) Day 5–30: retention touchpoints and signals
   - Who: Manager + People Ops
   - Action: manager 1:1 at day 7; People Ops pulse at day 14 (short survey); manager + peer check at day 30. Capture any residual blockers and early wins.

Templates (copy-paste and personalize):
- Written offer email (T0+0–4h):
  Subject: Redwood Inference — Offer for {{role}}
  Hi {{candidate_name}},

  Congratulations — we are excited to offer you the role of {{role}} at Redwood Inference. Attached is your formal offer letter (PDF) which includes compensation, title, manager, and proposed start window ({{start_window}}). Please review and sign following the instructions at the bottom of the letter.

  If you have any questions about benefits, relocation, or the contract itself, reply to this email and I’ll help coordinate answers. Our goal is to make this process smooth — we recommend reviewing within 72 hours if possible.

  Best,
  {{recruiter_name}}

- Manager welcome note (T0+24–48h):
  Subject: Welcome note from your manager at Redwood
  Hi {{candidate_name}},

  Quick note to say I’m thrilled we extended an offer for {{role}}. I’d love to connect briefly during your first week to talk about priorities and the team. If you have any questions before signing, feel free to ping me.

  — {{manager_name}}

- Post-sign checklist email (T_sign+0–4h):
  Subject: Next steps — Welcome to Redwood Inference
  Hi {{candidate_name}},

  Thank you for signing! A few items to help us get you ready for day 1:
  1) Complete background check form: {{bg_link}}
  2) Upload ID and tax documents to {{secure_portal}}
  3) Confirm laptop preference survey: {{hw_link}}
  4) Share preferred pronouns and timezone for scheduling

  Our People Ops partner {{ops_name}} will reach out to schedule logistics and answer questions. If you need relocation or visa help, let us know and we’ll connect you to the mobility specialist.

  Welcome aboard!

  — People Ops

Communication channels and orchestration notes:
- Use ATS status tags to drive cadence triggers (verbal-offer, offer-sent, signed, preboarding-ready).
- Automate the routine emails where possible, but enforce a human check at these nodes: written-offer (send), post-sign confirmation, day-3 check-in, pre-day-0 handoff.
- Maintain a single source of truth: new-hire tracker (sheet) with acceptance date, start date, equipment, relocation required flag, and readiness flag.

Risk signals and escalation:
- Candidate silence >72 hours after written offer: recruiter follows up with phone and Slack DM template.
- Candidate lists multiple open offers or asks for extended decision window >14 days: flag for hiring manager to proactively engage with growth/comp package conversation.
- Background-check delays beyond 7 business days: People Ops flag to manager and offer contingency plan for earlier start with limited access if policy allows.

Operational checklist for handoff to onboarding (fields to include in handoff email):
- Candidate name, role, manager, start date
- Signed offer date and copy link
- Equipment requested and shipping address
- Background-check status and expected completion date
- Visa/relocation notes + contacts
- Special accommodations or accessibility needs

Data capture: minimal required fields in ATS or sheet:
- source, recruiter, hiring manager, offer_sent_at, accepted_at, start_date, bg_check_status, equipment_status, relocation_flag, readiness_flag, decline_reason (if applicable)

Open questions / action items for review:
- Define SLA for recruiter manager follow-ups for offers older than 7 days.
- Decide which emails can be fully automated vs. templated-but-sent-manually.
- Agree on privacy-safe ways to capture candidate feedback (pulse survey) at day 14.

Appendix — quick Slack DM template (use when candidate is unresponsive after 72h):
  Hi {{candidate_name}} — this is {{recruiter_name}} from Redwood Inference. I wanted to check in about the offer we sent on {{offer_date}}. Do you need any additional information or time? Happy to hop on a quick call.

Notes on tone and accessibility:
- Keep messages concise, empathetic, and choice-forward.
- Offer options (call, calendar invite, docs) rather than prescriptive deadlines where possible.
- Translate key emails for non-native English speakers on request (recruiter to arrange).
